Initially, the water begins to saturate the leaf, enhancing its color and causing it to become more pliable. As the washing progresses, the leaf becomes increasingly limp, conforming to the shape of the hands that manipulate it. By the final frame, the leaf is fully unfurled and uniformly wet, with the water having cleansed its entire surface. This sequence captures the transition from a dry, possibly unwashed leaf, to one that is prepared for consumption or further culinary use.
